question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $18,$ the additive inverse of $11$ modulo $18$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $11$ modulo $18$ is the integer $0\le x<18$ such that

$$
x+11≡0\,(\text{mod}\,18).
$$

Notice that $-11+11≡0,$ so $x≡-11\,(\text{mod}\,18).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-11 & \,(\text{mod}\,18) \\  & ≡0-11 & \,(\text{mod}\,18) \\  & ≡18-11 & \,(\text{mod}\,18) \\  & ≡7 & \,(\text{mod}\,18)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $11$ modulo $18$ is $7.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
7+11≡18≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,18)
$$

**Note:** The additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
